content.what_it_is: Python (numpy/matplotlib) counterpart of plot_solitary.m for the FUNWAVE-TVD surface_wave_1d case, apparently prepared for a postprocessing workshop (fdir points to /Users/Gaby/Desktop/Postprocessing-Workshop/..., L9). Reconstructs the 1-D beach analytically: m=1024 points at dx=1.0 (L11-12), x list comprehension (L18), depth array allocated as np.zeros((m,m))+10.0 (L19) though only column 0 is ever used; the loop over i (L21-25) leaves depth at 10.0 for i < Xslp (no-op assignment L23) and applies dep[i,0]=10-(x[i]-Xslp)*SLP with SLP=0.05, Xslp=750.0 beyond (L25). DEP = dep*-1 converts to elevation with negative below MWL (L27). For each snapshot in files=[1,6,11,17] (L30) it loads eta_<5-digit> (L42) into a 4x1 subplot grid (L44), plotting bottom profile DEP[:,0] in black and the first row eta[0,:] in blue (L46) with axis [0, 1024, -1.5, 1.5] (L50) and a title 'Time = <files[num]*10> sec' (L52-53). The single figure (figsize=(7,8), dpi=600, L36) is saved as eta_1d_solitary.png (L57).
entities: fdir — hardcoded workshop data directory, L9
m — number of grid points, L11
length — 8, L32 (unused; shadows built-in len-style name)

equations.ref: depth-to-elevation sign flip (comment: negative under MWL=0)

verbatim_spans.text: DEP = dep*-1  # - values are under MWL=0, + values are over MWL=0

unresolved: dep is allocated as a full m x m array (L19) though only column 0 is read/written (L23, L25, L46) — mirrors the MATLAB zeros(m) square-matrix quirk of plot_solitary.m at the cost of an unnecessary 1024x1024 array
the slope condition compares the integer index i to the position Xslp in meters (if i < Xslp, L22) — equivalent to comparing x[i] only because dx=1.0 (L12); would misplace the toe for other dx
the plotted eta is eta[0,:] (first row, L46), implying the loaded eta_ files are 2-D with the 1-D profile in row 0; file layout is not documented here
wid (L31) and length (L32) are assigned but never used — figure size is hardcoded as figsize=(7,8) (L36); comment '# Locate Wavemaker and sponge' (L29) has no associated code
time in the title is files[num]*10 (L52), asserting a 10 s output interval not read from any input
